terms.gloss: a sailing, a voyage; a trip by boat
evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.4: tum, mī Tīrō, cōnsulitō nāvigātiōnī
Cic. Fam. 13.68.1: cursūs nāvigātiōnum tuārum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for any trip by water, long or short. For a short outing by boat the verb is as natural: nāviculā vehī, or excurrere (see “excursion”).

phrases.latin: Hodiē post merīdiem nāviculā vehēmur. Vīsne?
phrases.english: This afternoon we’ll go out in a boat. Would you like to?
It’ll be a short boat trip: about an hour.

phrases.latin: tum, mī Tīrō, cōnsulitō nāvigātiōnī: nūllā in rē jam tē festīnāre volō
phrases.english: then, my Tiro, take thought for the voyage: I don’t want you to hurry over anything now
we went down to our boats

sources: Lewis & Short: navigatio · Lewis & Short: navicula
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 206.
